promise.en: By the end, you can describe your room, your school or your town.
promise.mn: Энэ хичээлийн төгсгөлд өрөө, сургууль, хотоо дүрсэлж чадна.

slides.say: There is and there are. This is how English tells someone what is in a place. By the end of this video you can describe your room, your school or your town.

explain.en: To say what is in a place, English starts with there.
explain.mn: Хаана юу байгааг хэлэхдээ англиар there-ээр эхэлнэ.

slides.say: Read each caption twice. Then: when we tell someone what is in a place, English starts the sentence with there. And look: sometimes there is, sometimes there are. Why?
slides.teach: Describing a picture is one of the main things students are asked to do in English, at school and in speaking practice, so this structure pays off immediately.

rows.en: There's a bed in my room.
There is milk in the fridge.

callout.en: In a list, the first thing decides: There is a bed and two chairs.
callout.mn: Жагсаахад эхний зүйл шийднэ: There is a bed and two chairs.

slides.say: Count first. One thing: there is, and in speaking, there's. [click] More than one: there are. [click] Things you can't count, like milk or water, also take there is. [click] And when you list several things, look only at the first one. A bed first: there is. Two chairs first: there are.
slides.teach: There are has no written short form; there're exists in speech but don't teach it for writing. The "first thing decides" rule is how people really speak; in very formal writing some prefer are for any list, but students will hear the first-thing pattern constantly.

callout.en: The place comes first in Mongolian and last in English.
callout.mn: Байршил монголоор эхэнд, англиар төгсгөлд ордог.

slides.say: Look at the order. In Mongolian the place comes first and байна comes last. [click] In English it is the opposite: there is first, then the thing, and the place goes at the end. [click] Place at the front in Mongolian, at the back in English.
slides.teach: This is exactly where Mongolian speakers produce In my room is a bed or In my room has a bed. If a student wants the place first, English still needs there: In my room, there is a bed. Say that as one spoken line.

cards.en: There **isn't** a TV in my room.
There **aren't** any chairs in the kitchen.

explain.en: There's no means the same as there isn't a.
explain.mn: There's no, there isn't a хоёр утга нэг.

slides.say: For the negative: isn't and aren't. With a plural, English usually adds any: There aren't any chairs. [click] And a very common second way: There's no TV. It means the same as There isn't a TV.
slides.teach: Keep no and isn't as two equal choices. Students who mix them produce There isn't no TV; if you want, say once that English uses only one negative word.

rows.mn: Энд ойрхон цэцэрлэгт хүрээлэн байна уу?

rows.en: **How many** students **are there** in your class? [down]
rows.mn: Танай ангид хэдэн сурагч байдаг вэ?

callout.en: Your voice goes up for yes or no questions, and down for How many.
callout.mn: Тийм, үгүй асуултад дуу дээшилнэ, How many-д доошилно.

slides.say: For a question, swap there and is: Is there a park near here? The short answer keeps there: Yes, there is. [click] Same with plurals, and again with any. [click] And to ask about a number: How many, then a plural noun, then are there. Listen to the voice: up for yes or no questions, down for How many.
slides.teach: How many always takes a plural noun and are there; say the pattern twice as a chunk: How many ... are there?

title.mn: there is үү, it is үү?

rows.en: **There is** a park near my house.
rows.mn: Манай байрны ойролцоо цэцэрлэгт хүрээлэн бий.

rows.en: **There are** two cats in our flat.

callout.en: there is says something new is there.
callout.mn: there is: шинэ зүйл байгааг хэлнэ.

slides.say: There is brings something new into the conversation. Once it is there, we describe it with it or they. First there, then it. There is a park near my house. It is very big.
slides.teach: Mongolian байна covers both "exists" and "is", which is why students say It is a park near my house. Showing the two sentences working together is how real English flows, and it fixes the mistake by giving each structure its own job.

context.en: Mongolian puts the place first. English starts with There is.
context.mn: Монголоор: Миний өрөөнд ор байна. Англиар: There is a bed in my room.

right.en: **There is** a bed in my room.

mistakes.wrong: ~~It is~~ a park near my house.

right.en: **There is** a park near my house.
right.mn: Манай байрны ойролцоо цэцэрлэгт хүрээлэн бий.

slides.say: First: count, then choose. [click] Second: the Mongolian order. There is goes first, the place goes last. [click] Third: a new thing needs there is, not it is.
slides.teach: The three mistakes come from slides 3, 4 and 7. The second is the most deeply Mongolian of the three and is worth reading twice.

lines.en: Our school is in the centre of the city.
**There are** 30 classrooms and a big library.
lines.mn: 30 анги, бас том номын сан бий.

lines.en: **There's** a gym next to the library. It's new.
lines.mn: Номын сангийн хажууд биеийн тамирын заал бий. Шинэ заал.

lines.en: **There isn't** a swimming pool, but **there are** two sports fields.
lines.mn: Усан сан байхгүй ч хоёр спорт талбай бий.

lines.en: How many students **are there**? **There are** about 900.

slides.say: Read each line twice. Point out there's a gym followed by It's new, the negative with but, and the How many question answered in the same line.
slides.teach: Every structure in the lesson appears once. Students can rewrite it about their own school or their own town straight away.

cards.mn: There is + нэг · There are + олон

cards.en: There is a bed **in my room**: the place goes at the end.

slides.say: Line one: count first. One thing: there is. More than one: there are. In a list, the first thing decides. [click] Line two: the order is the opposite of Mongolian. There is comes first and the place goes at the end: There is a bed in my room. [click] Line three: there is brings something new into the conversation, and it describes it after that. There is a park near my house. It is very big. Close: Now you can describe your room, your school or your town, and ask what is in a place and how many there are.
slides.teach: On line two, say the Mongolian sentence and the English sentence one after the other so the order flip is heard, not just seen.

slides.say: Closing line: Одоо энэ видеоны доорх дасгалаар мэдлэгээ шалгаарай.
slides.teach: Say the closing line, then hold the slide silently for three seconds.
